title: Genome-wide association studies of missing metabolite measures from two population-based studies.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: read the abstract and data availability statement in the open-access full text. The Europe PMC supplementary file listing timed out (supplement not retrievable). The GWAS Catalog legacy REST query by PubMed ID returned HTTP 410 (endpoint gone), so I could not confirm that summary-statistics accession GCP001677 resolves.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cohort sizes (NEO, the Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study, N=594; Rhineland Study, N=4,165), 224 metabolites missing in 10-90% of people, 55 significant associations, and that summary statistics are deposited in the GWAS Catalog as GCP001677.

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level genotype and metabolomics data for both cohorts are available only on request to the NEO Executive Board and the Rhineland Study data access committee (paper text). Only GWAS summary statistics are public, and I did not confirm they resolve.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The natural label, whether each person's metabolite value is missing, exists only in the restricted individual-level data. Public summary statistics are per-SNP association results, so any label would have to be built from them.

a5_enough_rows.note: 4,759 individuals per the paper, but none are accessible. The 224 metabolites or 41 lead SNPs in the public output are too few to train on.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not check: no files opened.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label taken from public summary statistics would be the output of a statistical model (GWAS p-values and effect sizes), not a direct measurement.

honest_claim_h3: Without individual-level data, no model can claim to predict a person's metabolite missingness. Only per-SNP summary association results are public.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's genetic variants to predict which blood metabolites will be undetectable in their mass spectrometry profile.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes and metabolite detection calls for 4,759 people in two German and Dutch cohorts (count from the paper; the data are access-restricted).
plain_idea.predict: Whether each of 224 metabolites is missing (below detection) in that person's untargeted mass spectrometry measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Metabolomics analysts could treat genetically driven missingness as signal instead of imputing it away. That value depends on getting the data.

ml_idea: Predict per-person metabolite missingness from genotype. This is not feasible without an access application to both cohorts.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement: individual-level data are on request only.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 (data must download). Individual-level genotype and metabolomics data from both cohorts (NEO and the Rhineland Study) need an access request. Only GWAS summary statistics are public, so there is no per-person label to train on.
